name: Build - knetscan-init

on:
  push:
    branches: [ main ]
    paths:
      - 'knetscan-init/**'
      - '.github/workflows/build-knetscan-init.yml'

env:
  GO_VERSION: '1.22'

jobs:
  build-knetscan-init:
    name: Build knetscan-init
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
    - name: Checkout code
      uses: actions/checkout@v4

    - name: Set up Go
      uses: actions/setup-go@v5
      with:
        go-version: ${{ env.GO_VERSION }}

    - name: Cache Go modules
      uses: actions/cache@v4
      with:
        path: |
          ~/.cache/go-build
          ~/go/pkg/mod
        key: ${{ runner.os }}-go-${{ env.GO_VERSION }}-knetscan-init-${{ hashFiles('knetscan-init/go.sum') }}

    - name: Install Go tools
      run: |
        go install github.com/golangci/golangci-lint/cmd/golangci-lint@v1.55.2

    - name: Build knetscan-init
      run: |
        cd knetscan-init
        make build-all

name: Build - knetscan-wf

on:
  push:
    branches: [ main ]
    paths:
      - 'knetscan-wf/**'
      - 'knetscan/**'  # Also trigger when knetscan changes (dependency)
      - '.github/workflows/build-knetscan-wf.yml'

env:
  GO_VERSION: '1.22'

jobs:
  build-knetscan-wf:
    name: Build knetscan-wf
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
    - name: Checkout code
      uses: actions/checkout@v4

    - name: Set up Go
      uses: actions/setup-go@v5
      with:
        go-version: ${{ env.GO_VERSION }}

    - name: Cache Go modules
      uses: actions/cache@v4
      with:
        path: |
          ~/.cache/go-build
          ~/go/pkg/mod
        key: ${{ runner.os }}-go-${{ env.GO_VERSION }}-knetscan-wf-${{ hashFiles('knetscan-wf/go.sum') }}

    - name: Install Go tools
      run: |
        go install github.com/golangci/golangci-lint/cmd/golangci-lint@v1.55.2

    - name: Build knetscan-wf
      run: |
        cd knetscan-wf
        # Replace knetscan dependency with local version for GitHub Actions
        go mod edit -replace=github.com/NVIDIA/knetscan/knetscan=../knetscan
        go mod tidy
        make build-all

# KNetScan
## A Kubernetes scalable port discovery and reachability analyzer

* Performs comprehensive port scans across all pods, services, and nodes (both internal and external IPs)
* Intelligently optimized port collection to limit the port scans, enabling rapid scans on large clusters
* Highly configurable targeting - specify namespaces, nodes, selective ports, or specific IP ranges to scan
* Rich output formats including interactive network graphs, Jupyter notebooks, Elasticsearch integration, and Grafana dashboard support
* Internal and external network visibility - deploy both inside and outside the cluster to scan targets within the cluster and on external networks, helping validate ingress and egress rules
* Flexible scheduling options - run one-time assessments or continuous monitoring with regular automated scans
* Advanced scanning techniques - initiates SYN scans by default with automatic fallback to CONNECT scans on failure

## Repository Structure

This repository contains several components:

- **knetscan**: Kubernetes resource discovery and port scanning engine
- **knetscan-init**: DaemonSet for discovery of open ports on nodes
- **knetscan-wf**: Workflow orchestrator that automates the entire scanning process - deploys components, coordinates scans, collects results, and generates visualizations (similar to a Kubernetes Operator)

## High Level Design

![Workflow Architecture](docs/workflow-arch-diag.png)

*Figure: Knetscan-workflow architecture*

![Tool Architecture](docs/simplistic-arch-diag.png)

*Figure: Knetscan tool architecture*

## Deployment Options

KNetScan offers two primary ways to deploy and use the tool:

### Option 1: Using knetscan-wf (Recommended)

This approach is the simplest way to run KNetScan. [knetscan-wf](knetscan-wf/README.md) automates the entire process, running both external and internal scans, and generating visualization outputs.

The workflow orchestrator sequentially performs the following:
- Runs external scans against your cluster
- Deploys KNetScan-Init to discover open ports
- Deploys KNetScan for internal scanning
- Collects and combines all results
- Generates network graphs and Jupyter notebooks
- Cleans up all resources when done

#### Workflow Results

After running KNetScan using the workflow orchestrator, you'll find these outputs in your results directory (see examples at [docs/wf/sample-output](docs/wf/sample-output)):

* Raw JSON scan results for both internal and external scans
* Interactive network graph in HTML format
* Jupyter notebook for advanced queries and analysis
* Visualization resources (JavaScript, CSS)

### Option 2: Custom Deployment (For Advanced Users)

If you need more control over the scanning process, you can run the internal and external scanners separately.

The external scanner:
- Runs from outside the cluster
- Scans externally accessible IPs and services
- Uses kubeconfig to access cluster information (targets can be overridden via command-line arguments)

The internal scanner:
- Intended to be run as a DaemonSet
- Scans from each node to all the discovered targets across the cluster
- If not using knetscan-init (included as part of the knetscan workflow), knetscan will simply leverage the information it gathers from the K8s API to determine the targets - All internal pod, service, and node IPs.


For more detailed information about each component, see the README files in their respective directories.

## Quick Start

Goto [knetscan-wf README](knetscan-wf/README.md)

# KNetScan
## A Kubernetes Network Scanner

![image](resources/simplistic-arch-diag.png)

*[Refer to the website for detailed architecture diagrams]*

Gain visibility on your Kubernetes cluster network using this tool.
 * Fetch available pods, services, and node IPs - cluster and external, and run port scans on each.
 * Port scan initiates CONNECT scans by default, and falls back to SYN scans on failure.
 * Run the tool inside or outside the target cluster.
 * Configure it to check for specific namespaces or nodes.
 * Check egress rules by deploying inside the cluster and setting an external target on an internet.
 * One-time scans or regular scans for monitoring.

## Building from Source

```bash
cd knetscan/knetscan

# Build the binary
make build-all
```

## Using Docker

```bash
# Build the Docker image
make docker-build
```

## Deployment Models

**Internal Scanner:**
* Intended to be run inside a Kubernetes cluster.
* Uses Kubernetes client to fetch all IPs (pods, services, and nodes) and then run nmap scans on their internal and external IPs.
* With the `add-scan-ips` argument add target IPs/domains to check for your cluster's egress rules.
* Any dashboard (Grafana, Kibana, etc) can be used to visualize relevant data.

**External Scanner:**
* Intended to be run outside a Kubernetes cluster. Expects path to the kubeconfig (for the target cluster) as input.
* Fetches all relevant external IPs (services and nodes) and then run nmap scans on their external IPs.
* Database and dashboard options remain the same.

## Command Line Arguments

| Argument | Data type | Description |
| -------- | --------- | ----------- |
| version | bool | Display knetscan version information and exit |
| one-time | bool | Run the scan only once |
| freq | int | Scan frequency in minutes (if not a one-time scan) |
| in-cluster | bool | Is the code deployed inside the target cluster |
| kubeconfig | string | Absolute path to the kubeconfig to access the target cluster (if not deployed inside the target cluster) |
| local-storage-only | bool | Post data to local storage only (Elasticsearch is ignored) |
| local-storage-path | string | Path to store results in local storage |
| scan-if-no-ports | bool | Run the default nmap scan behavior if no ports are found by knetscan |
| scan-ports-override | string | Override the default ports to be scanned by nmap (Provide in nmap compliant format - "1,2,4-6") |
| add-targets-file | string | File containing additional targets to scan. Generally from knetscan-init container |
| add-scan-targets | string | Add target CIDRs:Ports to scan. Note - In this argument the values are separated by a semicolon to allow use of comma for ports. Ideally used to test egress rules. (format - "192.168.0.1:1-2;google.com:443;10.0.0.0/24:4-10") |
| skip-auto-detect | bool | Skip fetching IPs from api-server and only scan the IPs provided in 'add-scan-targets' |
| single-host-scan-timeout | int | Override the recommended 60 seconds per host scan timeout |
| namespaces | string | Restrict the scan to specific namespaces (Provide in format - "ns1,ns2,ns3") |
| nodes | string | Restrict the scan to specific nodes (Provide in format - "node1,node2") |
| es | string | Elasticsearch endpoint |
| es-user | string | Elasticsearch username |
| es-pass | string | Elasticsearch password |
| es-ca-fp | string | Elasticsearch certificate fingerprint |
| es-index | string | Elasticsearch index for posting scan results (default: knetscan-index) |
| log-dir | string | Directory where the log file resides. If not specified, logs to stderr |
| log-format | string | Defines the logging mode to either console or json |
| log-level | string | Defines the logging level. Choose from one of: fatal, error, warn, info, debug |

## Example Usage

### Running inside a cluster

```bash
# Create a namespace for knetscan
kubectl create ns knscan

# Run knetscan
helm install -f charts/knetscan/values.yaml knetscan charts/knetscan/. --namespace=knscan
```

### Running outside a cluster

```bash
# Run directly on your system
sudo ./knetscan -one-time=true -in-cluster=false -local-storage-only=true -local-storage-path=$HOME/knetscan-results -kubeconfig=$HOME/.kube/config
```

### Important configuration differences for external scanner

1. `in-cluster` must be set to `false` (tells the program that it's run outside the target cluster)
2. `kubeconfig` must be provided (provides access to the target cluster's api-server)
3. `local-storage-path` should be set to save the results locally

## Using with Visualization Tools

The scan results can be visualized using tools like Grafana. A sample dashboard template is provided at [/resources/sample-grafana-dashboard.json](resources/sample-grafana-dashboard.json).

For a more comprehensive approach with automated visualization, consider using the KNetScan Workflow tool which automatically generates network graphs and Jupyter notebooks.

# KNetScan Workflow

KNetScan Workflow is an orchestration tool that automates the complete port scanning process for Kubernetes clusters using knetscan and knetscan-init. It simplifies deployment by running all necessary components in the right sequence and collecting results for visualization.

## What KNetScan Workflow Does

1. Runs external scans from your machine (outside the cluster) against your target cluster
2. Deploys KNetScan Init as a DaemonSet in the cluster to discover listening ports
3. Deploys KNetScan for internal scanning
4. Collects all results from both scans
5. Generates visualization resources (network graph and Jupyter notebook)
6. Cleans up all resources when complete
7. Provides fault tolerance with proper cleanup on errors or interruptions

## Prerequisites

**Your system needs:**
1. `kubectl` installed and configured with admin access to the target cluster
2. `nmap` installed for external scans - https://nmap.org/download
3. Go 1.22.0+
4. `knetscan` binary (steps detailed below)

**The target cluster needs:**
1. `knetscan` and `knetscan-init` images available in a registry (steps detailed below)
2. Update the registry in helm values files if using custom images (steps detailed below)

### Step 1: Setting Up Docker Images

Before running the workflow, you need to build and push the knetscan and knetscan-init Docker images to a registry accessible by your cluster:

```bash
# Clone this repo
git clone https://github.com/NVIDIA/knetscan.git; cd knetscan

# Set your registry (replace with your actual registry)
export REGISTRY=your-registry.com

# Build and push both images (includes both amd64 and arm64)
cd knetscan
make docker-push

cd ../knetscan-init  
make docker-push
```

### Step 2: Configuring Image Registry in knetscan-wf

Update the embedded values files to use your registry:

```bash
# Edit knetscan values
vi knetscan-wf/values.yaml
# Update: image.repository: your-registry.com/knetscan
# Update: image.tag: v0.0.1  # Use your actual version

# Edit knetscan-init values  
vi knetscan-wf/values-init.yaml
# Update: image.repository: your-registry.com/knetscan-init
# Update: image.tag: v0.0.1  # Use your actual version
```

*Alternatively, you can create custom values files and use the `-values-yaml` and `-init-values-yaml` command-line options.*

### Step 3: Building knetscan binary (skip if Step 1 completed)

The knetscan-wf requires the knetscan binary for external scanning. Step 1's `make docker-push` automatically builds this binary, so you only need this step if you skipped Step 1.

```bash
cd knetscan
make build-all
```

## Quick Start

```bash
# Build knetscan-wf (assumes knetscan binary built per prerequisites)
cd knetscan-wf
make build-all

# Run the workflow (using v0.0.1 as example version)
sudo ./build/v0.0.1/linux-amd64/knetscan-wf \
  -kubeconfig=$HOME/.kube/config \
  -work-dir=/tmp/knetscan-results \
  -exec-path=../knetscan/build/v0.0.1/linux-amd64/knetscan \
  -docker-config=$HOME/.docker/config.json  # Required for accessing container registry during deployment
```
#### Note 1: The docker config file must contain credentials to pull the knetscan and knetscan-init images pushed in [Step 1 from the Prerequisites section](#step-1-setting-up-docker-images) above.
#### Note 2: Replace `linux-amd64` with `darwin-amd64`, `linux-arm64`, or `darwin-arm64` as needed for your platform. Replace `v0.0.1` with your actual version (extracted from git tag).
#### Note 3: MacOS users may need to remove quarantine attributes from the binaries to allow execution
```bash
sudo xattr -rd com.apple.quarantine ./build/v0.0.1/linux-amd64/knetscan-wf
sudo xattr -rd com.apple.quarantine ../knetscan/build/v0.0.1/linux-amd64/knetscan
```

## Command Line Arguments

| Argument | Data type | Description |
| -------- | --------- | ----------- |
| version | bool | Display knetscan-wf version information and exit |
| kubeconfig | string | Absolute path to kubeconfig - When deployed outside the cluster |
| work-dir | string | Path to directory in which workflow related files would be created |
| exec-path | string | Path to the knetscan executable. Default - './knetscan' |
| skip-scan | string | Skip one of the scan types - internal or external. Format - '-skip-scan internal OR -skip-scan external' |
| docker-config | string | Absolute path to the docker config file that provides access to the container repo. Default - $HOME/.docker/config.json |
| ext-scan-ports | string | Override the default ports scanned by the external scanner(Provide in nmap compliant format - "1,2,4-6") |
| init-values-yaml | string | Absolute path to the Knetscan-init chart values.yaml file for internal scan. If not provided, default settings would be used for the scan |
| values-yaml | string | Absolute path to the Knetscan chart values.yaml file for internal scan. If not provided, default settings would be used for the scan |
| helm-cache-path | string | Helm cache path. If not provided, will use helm's default values |
| helm-config-path | string | Helm config path. If not provided, will use helm's default values |
| only-parse-path | string | If mentioned, all scans will be skipped. KNetScan output .json files at this path will be used to generate cleansed results. Results posted at the same path |
| ignore-scan-fails | bool | Removes the scan failures from the generated results |
| log-dir | string | Directory where the log file resides. If not specified, logs to stderr |
| log-format | string | Defines the logging mode to either console or json |
| log-level | string | Defines the logging level. Choose from one of: fatal, error, warn, info, debug |

## Output Structure

After running the workflow, the results will be in the specified work directory with this structure:

```
/work-dir/knetscan/<timestamp>/
├── external/
│   └── <scan-results>.json    # Raw JSON output from external scans
├── internal/
│   └── <scan-results>.json    # Raw JSON output from internal scans
├── results/
│   ├── d3.v7.min.js
│   ├── network.js
│   └── network-graph.html     # Interactive network visualization
└── KNetScan-Queries.ipynb     # Jupyter notebook for advanced queries
```

## Using the Network Graph

Open the `network-graph.html` file in any web browser to visualize the network connections discovered by KNetScan. This interactive graph shows:

- Nodes representing Kubernetes resources
- Connections representing open network paths
- Port information on connections
- Filtering options for better analysis

## Using the Jupyter Notebook

To use the generated Jupyter notebook for advanced analysis:

1. Install [Jupyter](https://jupyter.org/install)
2. Install the [Go Kernel](https://github.com/gopherdata/gophernotes) for Jupyter
3. Run `jupyter lab` in the results directory
4. Open `KNetScan-Queries.ipynb` and run the cells
5. Customize queries as needed for your specific analysis needs

# KNetScan Init
## Discovery Component for KNetScan

KNetScan Init collects the open ports on Kubernetes nodes by running as a privileged container on the host network. This information is then used by the main KNetScan tool to perform targeted scans, significantly improving scan performance.

## Purpose

This component is deployed as a DaemonSet in the Kubernetes cluster to:

1. Run on each node in the cluster
2. Discover all listening ports on each node
3. Output the discovered ports to a shared directory
4. Allow KNetScan to target only relevant ports for scanning

## Build using Docker

```bash
# Build the Docker image
make docker-build
```

## Example Usage

KNetScan Init is typically deployed automatically by the KNetScan Workflow (knetscan-wf), but you can also deploy it manually using its helm chart under charts/knetscan-init.

## Integration with KNetScan

When using the knetscan workflow (knetscan-wf), KNetScan Init is typically deployed automatically. The workflow will:

1. Deploy KNetScan Init as a DaemonSet
2. Wait for all pods to complete discovery
3. Collect the discovered ports
4. Use this data to configure KNetScan for an optimized scan
5. Clean up the KNetScan Init resources when the scan is complete

# KNetScan Helm Chart

## Installation

Before installing the chart, you need to fetch the Elasticsearch dependency:

```bash
# Add the Elastic Helm repository
helm repo add elastic https://helm.elastic.co

# Download the Elasticsearch chart dependency
helm dependency update
```

This will download the Elasticsearch chart (elasticsearch-7.17.3.tgz) into the `charts/` directory.

To install the chart:

```bash
helm install knetscan ./charts/knetscan # add the values file as needed
```
